keenable.snippet:
# Kymera’s oral eczema drug impresses analysts with Dupixent-like phase 2 efficacy
Kymera Therapeutics’ phase 2b eczema clinical trial has [hit](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/11/23/3408198/0/en/kymera-therapeutics-announces-positive-results-from-broaden2-phase-2b-clinical-trial-of-kt-621-a-first-in-class-oral-stat6-degrader-in-patients-with-moderate-to-severe-atopic-derma.html) its primary endpoint and exceeded analyst expectations, teeing up further development of an oral drug candidate that could challenge Dupixent in a range of indications.
Investigators randomized 244 adults and adolescents with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis to take one of three doses of the STAT6 degrader KT-621 or placebo once daily for 16 weeks. At the end of that period, the mean Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) score in the mid-dose cohort had fallen by 72%, compared to a 27% decline on placebo, achieving the trial’s primary endpoint.
“Recognizing the limitation of cross-trial comparisons, the results were broadly comparable to marketed biologics and, importantly, the mid-dose was numerically superior to [Dupixent] on almost all endpoints,” Kymera CEO Nello Mainolfi, Ph.D., said on a conference call with investors.
In the mid-dose cohort, 62% of patients’ EASI scores improved by at least 75%, versus 22% in the placebo arm. The 40% placebo-adjusted result cleared the 30% delta that Guggenheim Securities analysts named as the bar for investor enthusiasm in a Nov. 22 note to investors.

The biotech linked the middle KT-621 dose to a 58% decline on the Peak Pruritus Numerical Rating Scale (PPNRS), which measures itching, compared to a 21% reduction on placebo. Kymera reported that 52% of patients on the middle dose had at least a 4-point reduction in PPNRS, versus 13% of their peers on placebo.

# Kymera oral eczema drug succeeds in Phase 2 trial
In the Phase 2 BROADEN2 trial, Kymera's pill KT-621 beat placebo on disease severity, itch and skin clearance. The middle dose produced a 45% placebo-adjusted improvement.
**By [Hana Sorensen](https://clinicalobserver.com/author/hana-sorensen)**, Biotech and trials correspondent
23 November 2026, 08:13 ET. 1-minute read.
Kymera Therapeutics announced Monday that its experimental pill KT-621 improved disease severity at 16 weeks in the Phase 2 BROADEN2 trial for moderate-to-severe eczema, [STAT reported](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/23/kymera-therapeutics-eczema-trial-success-potential-dupixent-rival/?utm_campaign=rss). The reduction compared with placebo was statistically significant across all three doses tested, according to the same report.
[STAT reported](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/23/kymera-therapeutics-eczema-trial-success-potential-dupixent-rival/?utm_campaign=rss) that the middle dose produced a peak placebo-adjusted improvement of 45%. At that dose, 62% of patients achieved at least a 75% improvement in disease severity, compared with 22% of the placebo group.
The trial also met its secondary endpoints, including reduced itch and a higher proportion of participants with clear or almost-clear skin, according to [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/23/kymera-therapeutics-eczema-trial-success-potential-dupixent-rival/?utm_campaign=rss). Kymera said the drug was generally safe and well tolerated. The only side effect more common in the KT-621 arms was conjunctivitis, reported in 20%, 13% and 11% of patients on the low, middle and high doses, respectively. [STAT reported](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/23/kymera-therapeutics-eczema-trial-success-potential-dupixent-rival/?utm_campaign=rss) that all cases were mild to moderate and none led to treatment discontinuation.

# Kymera shares jump 29% after positive midstage eczema trial
Investing.com -- shares rose 29% after the company reported positive Phase 2b results for KT-621, its experimental once-daily oral treatment for moderate to severe atopic dermatitis.
The 244-patient BROADEN2 trial met its primary and secondary endpoints at Week 16, with statistically significant improvements versus placebo across all three doses, the company said.
Patients receiving the mid dose recorded a 72% average reduction in eczema severity, measured by the Eczema Area and Severity Index, compared with 27% for placebo. Sixty-two percent achieved at least a 75% improvement in EASI scores, versus 22% on placebo. Clear or almost clear skin was reported in 38% of mid-dose patients, compared with 11% receiving placebo.
Kymera said improvements in eczema severity and itch emerged as early as Week 1. The mid dose consistently delivered the largest numerical improvements across efficacy measures.
KT-621 targets STAT6, a protein involved in Type 2 inflammation. The company believes the drug could offer disease control comparable to injectable biologics such as dupilumab, although BROADEN2 did not directly compare the treatments.
The drug was generally well tolerated over 16 weeks, according to Kymera. Conjunctivitis was the notable adverse-event imbalance, occurring in 13.1% of mid-dose patients. All cases in KT-621-treated patients were mild or moderate, and none led to treatment discontinuation.

The biotech linked the middle KT-621 dose to a 58% decline on the Peak Pruritus Numerical Rating Scale (PPNRS), which measures itching, compared to a 21% reduction on placebo. Investing.com -- shares rose 29% after the company reported positive Phase 2b results for KT-621, its experimental once-daily oral treatment for moderate to severe atopic dermatitis.

The drug was generally well tolerated over 16 weeks, according to Kymera. Conjunctivitis was the notable adverse-event imbalance, occurring in 13.1% of mid-dose patients. All cases in KT-621-treated patients were mild or moderate, and none led to treatment discontinuation.
